title: Story points considered harmful? 1 of 4 – Journey's start – Allan Kelly
summary: Allan Kelly opens a four-part look at 'story points considered harmful': points need a stable team, only work in aggregate, and humans cannot estimate.

assertions.quote: I don't believe story points can ever be stable if you don't have a stable team

verdicts.note: Consistent with Brooks's law and observed velocity volatility after staffing changes, though mostly practitioner data.

assertions.quote: They are a good predictor over several sprints but they offer no guarantees for the next sprint/iteration.

verdicts.note: Aggregate forecasting improves with history; per-sprint accuracy is poor in most reported data.

assertions.quote: we can't estimate. By “we” I mean humans.
in my book commitment and story pointing are alternatives

verdicts.note: A definitional stance on process design.
